# Rich text and the editorial blocks

How an article's text is drawn, the blocks an editor can put inside it (banner, code, media and
the editorial blocks: timeline, steps, key facts, outcome fork, diagram key, figure, chart, fact tabs),
the limits those share, and how agents write two of them as Markdown tags. [News](/src/modules/news/README.md) posts and [events](/src/modules/events/README.md) use it;
page-builder blocks are in the [site note](/src/modules/site/README.md). Props and where each
renderer is used: [rich-text components](/docs/reference/components/rich-text.md); the
rich-text fields of each collection: [content types](/docs/reference/content-types/README.md).

## Links between fields and values

- Limits of key facts, the timeline and fact tabs are written once (`editorial/editorialLimits.ts`); the block's fields, the Markdown tag's checks and the tests read them. A chart's limits are `CHART_LIMITS` in `src/platform/lib/chart/spec.ts`.
- Block slugs of key facts, fact tabs and outcome fork are written once (`editorial/blockTypes.ts`); their configs, the Markdown tags and the article-width rule match on them.
- Stored block to plain props: each `editorial/<block>.ts` maps the stored fields to what the renderer draws and drops items without a heading, title or value (decision 0013). `editorial/chart.ts` maps both ways between the stored rows (numbers, a hatching checkbox) and `ChartSpec`.
- `<Chart … />` and `<FactTabs … />` are written and read with one escaping (`editorial/editorialTag.ts`, `chartMarkdown.ts`, `factTabsMarkdown.ts`); the [agents](/src/modules/agents/README.md)' suggestions use them.
- Heading text to anchor id (`headingAnchors.ts`): the renderer's heading ids and the "On this page" menu (`articleToc.tsx`) both read it, so they match.
- A document's first heading becomes a hero title (`splitHeadingFromBody.ts`, used by `src/modules/site/ui/PageHero.tsx`).
- A chart block has a Colors choice: the usual colors or orange and gray (`palette`, `editorial/chartBaseFields.ts`, #856).
- A chart can be a breakdown (kind `breakdown`): a square value in dollars (or Hide the squares, for ranked bars only, #943) and up to seven areas, each with optional pieces; a piece marked Shown sits under its area, the others go in the smaller-pieces list (`editorial/chartBreakdownFields.ts`, #866).
- A chart part's key comes from its label (`editorial/chartKeys.ts`), so one part links across two groups' legends.

## Behaviors and events

- Text keeps the reading width. An article holding key facts, fact tabs or an outcome fork fills the column instead (`articleColumn.ts`, #774); post and event pages both call it.
- The "On this page" menu appears from three sections (`articleToc.tsx`, `src/platform/ui/onThisPage.ts`, #574). Only h2 and h3 count, and headings inside blocks get no anchor (`headingAnchors.ts`). A repeated heading gets `-2`, `-3`.
- A link to a page or post resolves to its site address; one with nowhere to go (a deleted document) shows as plain text (`RichText.tsx`, #215).
- A chart that fails its rules is left out of the page and logged, not allowed to break the article (`richTextBlocks.tsx`). The editor refuses it on save.
- A banner can be closed by the visitor and hidden after its end time; pages refresh every 10 minutes (`BannerBlock.tsx`).
- The media block has two placements: `section` (page builder, brings its own container) and `inline` (inside text, uses the shared figure gap) (`MediaBlock.tsx`, #541).
- Rich text is `flow-root`, so a floated figure stays inside the article's text and what follows never wraps around it (`RichText.tsx`, #816). With `besideFloat` (post and event pages give it when the article has a picture, #1023) it is not a box of its own, so its lines flow beside the article's floated picture, and a clearing end keeps what follows below both the picture and its own figures. A post that opens with key facts, fact tabs or an outcome fork (and the heading that introduces them) is split there (`splitLeadingWideBlocks`, `articleColumn.ts`): the opening is drawn first, then the picture, then the rest of the text with `anchorSource` set to the whole article so heading ids still match the menu, so no blank block is left beside a card row. A card row that comes after some text still starts below a picture that is taller than that text.
- The figure block holds an image, a title, a label, a short and a long caption, a width and an optional numbered key; the key marker list is shared with the diagram key (`editorial/diagramKeyBlockConfig.ts`). `editorial/figure.ts` leaves out empty text and passes the rest to the shared `Figure` (`FigureBlock.tsx`, #817). The block's Title names the small expand icon over the picture's corner that opens the larger view (#1156).
- A fact tab opens with its heading and, on the same line where it fits (on a narrow phone they wrap below it), its figure and how sure we are (shown once: the tab button leaves both to screen readers), then its first chart or timeline (the chart's title and takeaway left to screen readers, since the heading is its title), then the short definition, then the other pictures. A tab whose panel starts with a whole tax bill block (#1018, #1111) is drawn in one order, top to bottom, in one column on every width (`editorial/BillShare.client.tsx`, `src/platform/lib/billShare.ts`): the tab's heading (up to 48 characters, so a question such as "What does this mean for your property taxes?" fits, #1118; it may run to two lines on a phone), the block's one intro line, the Rough Estimator, the answer card (the same space sits under the intro, between the estimator and the answer, and between the cards below, one shared value `BILL_GAP`, the same space as between paragraphs of rich text, 20 px, #1142), the whole bill (its own card, holding the City's breakdown as a closed row under the City's own row, #1163), one card of two open-and-close rows (both closed on load), then the tab's other pictures (#1118). How sure we are shows once, as the badge in the answer card (a plain tab shows it beside the heading). **The Rough Estimator** card is orange and compact: no title is drawn (screen readers still hear it named Rough Estimator), and no intro line or notes (the tab draws those); it holds a home value box under its label "Enter your assessed value" (base-size text) with a check-mark button inside the box at its end, named "Estimate" for screen readers (#1110, #1048, #1087): while the typed value is not a new number the button is disabled, flat and muted; once it is, the button is accent-colored and slightly raised, the box's border takes the accent, and with reduced motion the button does not lift. The button is drawn 36 px with a 44 px tap area and sits an equal 6 px from the box's top, bottom and end, so on a phone it is right above the keyboard. The box holds the home's value in the latest year, the one a reader knows (#1121), and starts at the City's average home for that year; it stays as typed when the year changes. It groups the digits with commas as the reader types (whole dollars, cents cut, `Field.Money`). On the same row as the box, centred on it and never larger than it, are the tax years as one small joined control with an option for each priced year, showing the year numbers only, the picked year filled with the accent (`SegmentedControl`), under a short label, "Tax rates", on the line of the box's label, centred over the control (beside the box and stacked alike, #1121) and tied to the control as its group name; a card narrower than 16 rem stacks the label and control whole under the box before anything wraps. Nothing is drawn under it. Choosing one applies at once, with a half-second count of the amounts, and no scroll (`editorial/RoughEstimator.tsx`). **The answer card** (`editorial/BillAnswer.tsx`) has a top row with the label on the left, "City tax on an average home" while the home is the City's average and "City tax on your home" after the reader estimates another value, and the status badge on the right of the same row (a card too narrow for both puts the badge whole on its own line). Under it the City's tax on the home last estimated in the year chosen is the biggest text on the tab (`Text` variant `figure`) followed by a small "a year", then the City's increase in the estimator's accent, orange, as text that passes on the card (`accent-strong`; "Up $91 a year, about $7.58 a month", or "No increase" when the year's tax is not higher than the year before's; in the earliest of several years (when the next year's increase can be worked out) the line reads "Base year" in the primary green, with a hidden copy of the next year's line keeping the card as tall in both years, #1135; the same figures a tab's `{yearly}` and `{monthly}` use, from `figuresFor`, so they always agree), then one small sentence: "Average home: $500,300. The City is 37% of the whole bill." (left out after an estimate: it would only repeat the value the reader typed and a share the whole bill shows, #1183). The badge follows the chosen year: it says the year's stored note ("Proposed", first letter capital, no brackets) with the "not final" look, and a year with no note shows the stored certainty of the tab's fact, so the badge and the year control can never disagree. **The whole bill** sits in its own card and reads like a receipt (#1196): the title "Your whole bill" with no amount beside it, then one row for every body, the largest share first, so with today's rates Metropolitan Schools, City of Madison, Dane County, Madison College, MATC (the order follows the amounts for every year and home value, so a year with another rate can change it; equal shares keep City, schools, county, college, #1202; "Madison College" on a phone narrower than 24 rem, where the full name would not fit beside the amounts, the rest kept for screen readers, `BILL_BODY_SHORT_NAMES`), each with its name, its percent and its dollars (the percent, then a small gap, then the dollars flush right, as on a bill and as in the breakdown chart, #1163, #1184) and, under them, its own bar in its color, drawn like the City breakdown's rows. There is no segmented bar on top and there are no colour squares. The bars share one scale, the largest body's, so every bar's length is in proportion to the others, and the four rows are built the same way and are as tall as each other (`ShareBill`, `editorial/billShareView.ts`); the City's bar is the primary green and the others are neutral tones of different lightness. The total is the last row, "Total property tax" on the left and its amount under the rows' dollars, bold, under a stronger rule, and it flashes the accent once when a new bill has finished counting; the pie is not drawn, and there are no rows until the bill is whole. **The City's breakdown** is a row of the whole bill itself, directly under the City of Madison row wherever the City falls in the order, set in from the left with a line in the City's color down its side, and its amounts set in from the right (about the dollar column's width, `NESTED_AMOUNTS_INSET`), so they end before the bodies' amounts and are not read as part of the sum, the kit's `Disclosure` in its `listRow` look, a tinted, borderless button-like row with a chevron so it reads as clickable, its label a little larger than the receipt's rows and smaller than the rows below (`ShareBill`'s `nested`, `editorial/BreakdownRow.tsx`, #1163); until the bill is whole there is no City row, so it follows the line saying the bill can't be shown yet. It is closed when the tab loads, with scripting off too, and opens by itself after every estimate that changes the bill, when it is closed: once that bill has counted and its total's flash has ended (`TOTAL_PULSE_MS`, 0.3 seconds), 0.1 seconds later (`OPEN_AFTER_TOTAL_MS`, short enough that the reader has not yet reacted to the total; with reduced motion there is no count or flash, so 0.1 seconds after the estimate), and then it expands over 0.5 seconds (#1170, #1176). Another bill settling during the wait (a year switch) starts the wait over, a year switch alone never opens it, an estimate that changes nothing never arms it, an open row is left as it is, a row the reader closed opens again on the next new estimate, and once it has expanded the page scrolls as it does for a reader's opening, keeping the whole bill's heading under the sticky header (`editorial/useBreakdownAutoOpen.client.ts`, #1165, #1178). The bill's counting and its one flash per settled bill are `editorial/useBillCount.client.ts`. Each time it opens, by hand or by itself, the fill is readied before the row shows (from the summary's click, or just before it opens itself), and, once it has expanded (500 ms), its bars grow from empty to their length in one second while its dollar amounts count up from nothing, the percents staying put (`ScaledBreakdown`'s `fillKey`; with reduced motion, the final bars and amounts at once), and its bars are thinner than a breakdown's elsewhere (`compact`). "Your City tax breakdown" holds the tab's breakdown chart alone (its takeaway line first, then the split, its "See the smaller pieces" row and its estimate badge; the chart's title is left to screen readers, since the row's title is the heading, and the City's tax for the year is not repeated here because the answer card gives it with its increase, #1144; the tab's stacked chart by year is not drawn and only gives the answer card its tax and increase, `editorial/cityTax.ts`; the row is left out when the tab has no breakdown chart). **The two rows** under the whole bill are one card, split by divider lines, of the kit's `Disclosure` (`row` look), both closed when the tab loads, working without scripting and never moving what is above them when opened (`editorial/BillDetails.tsx`): "Why your bill may differ" (the notes: a list the editor words and orders, one short line each, with a condition that decides when it shows: always, when the tab has more than one year, in a year with a proposed rate, or when a rate is missing so the whole bill can't be shown; a note can use blanks the page fills in (`{year}`, `{years}`, `{bodies}`, and `{link}` where the note's own link goes), and Admin refuses a blank its condition can't fill. The starting list says it is a rough estimate by neighbors with AI help that is not official or tax advice, that the City's assessed value of the home may differ from the one entered, that credits, exemptions, who owns the home and the type of property change a real bill, which year's rates are used, that an earlier year's home value is assumed to have changed as much as the average home's, that the City's rate for a year with a proposed rate may change, and a link to send us a note. A note that is not showing still takes its room, hidden from everyone, so an open row never changes height when a year is chosen; then the tab's short text and its detail; `editorial/billShareNotes.ts`) and "Sources" (each source once: the tab's own source, the year's and the City breakdown's, the same link shown once; the breakdown's as-of line sits above the links, so the breakdown row itself shows only its Estimate badge and fine print, #1180). The row titles and the notes are fields of the whole-bill block (#1158), and the starting text (the titles "Your City tax breakdown", "Why your bill may differ" and "Sources", and the starting notes) is typed once, in `editorial/billShareDefaults.ts`: a new block starts with it, and a block stored before the fields existed shows it until it is saved. The page loads already estimated for the City's average home. Typing changes nothing on its own: the answer card, the whole bill, the rows and the sentence a screen reader hears (a status line) follow the value last estimated. The check-mark button is disabled until the typed value is a valid number different from the one shown, and Enter in the box presses it. Pressing it never scrolls the page, since the answer sits right below the box: the amounts count from the old to the new in 1.5 seconds, then the total row flashes the accent once and fades (`total-pulse` in `theme/tailwind.css`, #1051). Choosing a year counts them too, in half a second: the mill rates move from the old year's to the new one's, so the answer, the bar and the receipt move together, and the total flashes when the count ends (`editorial/rateBlend.ts`, `YEAR_COUNT_MS`, #1087); with reduced motion on there is no count and no flash (`platform/ui/motion.client.ts`, `useCountedNumber.client.ts`, #1068). The City's tax in the answer card, the breakdown and the tab's figures count along with the bill, the City's tax blending between the two years (#1096). Everything is drawn again in the browser for every home value and year, so each amount is the City's slice of the bill, in whole dollars, the lines adding up exactly to it, with the split unchanged; until a value is estimated they show the average home. A panel holds one to three pictures. In a tab without a whole tax bill, the tab's source link becomes the link on the first mention of its text in the definition, and a "Source:" line shows only when the definition never says it; with one, the source is in the Sources row. Its charts show no "Show the numbers" box and keep the table for screen readers (`editorial/FactTabs.tsx`, `editorial/definitionWithSource.ts`, #980).
- **One story for the two years (#1121):** the typed value is the home's value in the latest year; an earlier year prices the same home at its earlier value, the typed value times that year's average home over the latest year's (`homeInYear`), with the whole bill and the City's tax both for that value. The increase is one number, from the two priced years (`increaseIn`): the City's tax in the year less the year before's, each rounded to the dollar as the cards show it, so the later card less the earlier card is the line, for any home, and switching years moves the City's tax by exactly that. It is not taken from the chart's own stored figures, which the rates and average homes can differ from by a few dollars; the chart only says which part is the increase. A year with no average home leaves the value as typed and shows no increase. A tab with a whole tax bill can write `{yearly}` and `{monthly}` in its button's figure and its heading: the City's extra tax in a year and in a month (the answer card's increase, so the three always agree, and a month is the year divided by 12, to the cent), for the home last estimated and the year chosen. They count with the bill when Estimate is pressed or a year is chosen (#1096), and the page loads with the average home's figures, the tab's heading shown with scripting off too. Text without them shows as written, and a tab with no bill, or with no City chart whose columns are the tax years, keeps the placeholders as written (`editorial/billFigures.ts`, `BillFigures.client.tsx`, #1029).
- Every fact tab has a link of its own (#1097): the address ends with `#tab-` and the tab's label as a readable name, `-2` for a repeat (`editorial/tabAnchors.ts`, the shared `Tabs`); copy it from the address bar after choosing the tab, and opening it lands on that tab.
- A fact tab button shows only its label, centred on one line, in a button as wide and tall as the others; the figure and how sure we are are visually hidden text in the button, so screen readers still hear them, and the open panel shows both with its heading, below it on a narrow phone (a tab with a whole tax bill shows them in its answer card). A tab's label is at most `FACT_TABS_LIMITS.label` characters, and a label of that length keeps visible room in its button down to 320 px with four tabs (the buttons use the smallest type and tight spacing on a phone); labels already stored are not changed (`editorial/FactCard.tsx`, `editorial/FactTabs.tsx`, #1112, which reverses #856).
- Plain text for structured data (`toPlainText.ts`): blocks are separated by a blank line, then trimmed.

## Shared pieces it uses

- Renderers are passed in by the caller, so `RichText.tsx` imports no block and a block can hold rich text without an import cycle (#135). Post and event pages pass `richTextBlocks.tsx`.
- Posts offer banner, code, media and all editorial blocks; events offer the same without code (`blockConfigs.ts`: `RICH_TEXT_BLOCKS`, `EVENT_RICH_TEXT_BLOCKS`). The code block is kept and available to posts; no repository content uses it.
- The composition roots are `src/modules/news/cms/posts.ts` and `src/modules/events/cms/events.ts`, which pass the block lists to the editor.
- Chart drawing is `src/platform/ui/chart/`; the "On this page" menu is `src/platform/ui/OnThisPage.client.tsx` (both in the [UI kit note](/src/platform/ui/README.md)).
- Also used by [directory](/src/modules/directory/README.md) (FAQ answers and their `FAQPage` text) and by the [site note](/src/modules/site/README.md)'s hero and content blocks; rich-text colours come from [theme](/src/platform/theme/README.md) tokens.

## Rules and the tests that protect them

- A field of only spaces counts as empty (`editorial/filledText.ts`).
- List blocks count rows the way Admin sends them: a number during form building is the count, but on a real save a number is no rows (`editorial/rowCount.ts`, #676; `src/payload.config.rowCounts.test.ts`).
- A chart is validated as a whole and each reason shows under its field (`editorial/chartValidate.ts`, `chartValidate.test.ts`, `src/payload.config.chartBlock.test.ts`).
- A timeline has at most one "Next up" milestone, and status is never shown by colour alone: dot shape, connector and a word (`editorial/timelineBlockConfig.ts`, `timelineStatus.ts`, `timelineBlockConfig.test.ts`).
- A tag that breaks the block's rules is refused with the reasons, and text with quotes, braces or backslashes reads back unchanged (`chartMarkdown.test.ts`, `factTabsMarkdown.test.ts`, `src/payload.config.factTabsMarkdown.test.ts`).
- Mappers: `editorial/*.test.ts(x)`, `factTabs*.test.ts`. Article width: `articleColumn.test.ts`. Menu and ids: `articleToc.test.tsx`, `headingAnchors.test.ts`. Title split: `splitHeadingFromBody.test.ts`. Block lists and renderers: `RichText.test.tsx`, `richTextBlocks.test.tsx`, `src/payload.config.test.ts`.

## Boundaries

- May import `src/platform/ui`, `src/platform/lib`, `src/platform/payload` and the generated `@/payload-types`. Modules use it only where they compose it: the CMS configs and pages named above.
- Never put a block's size limit as a literal in its config: add it to `editorial/editorialLimits.ts`.

## Decisions

- [0013](/docs/architecture/decisions/0013-cms-content-through-mappers.md) (plain props from mappers), epic #506 (explainer blocks), #640 and #664 (Markdown tags).

## Known gaps

- #676: steps, outcome fork and diagram key accept a number in place of their list.
- Limits of steps, outcome fork and diagram key are literals in their configs, not in `editorial/editorialLimits.ts` (#843).
